text: Spark gives you a hundred executors. Then one group by, and the whole job slows to a crawl.
Picture a billion orders, spread across those executors.
To count by country, every row with the same key has to land in the same partition.
So data moves between executors. That movement is called the shuffle.
Send it over the network to another executor.
Every one of those steps costs time. The next stage can't start until all the data arrives, so its tasks just sit and wait.
The fix? Move less data. Or spread the work across more executors.
Filter rows and columns before the shuffle.
And avoid shuffles you don't need.
One powerful trick: broadcast the small table to every executor, and skip the shuffle entirely.
